reference_model.note: NASA 3D Resources 'Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover' (.glb, 4.99 MB, ~200k tris, Blender 4.2 export, metres). Repo README: 'These assets are free and without copyright.' Matches documents: wheel diameter 0.525 m (doc 52.5 cm), width 2.705 m (doc 2.7 m), length without arm 3.09 m (doc 'about 3 meters'), HGA mid-aft on the port side. Mast and arm are stowed (cruise pose). Contains a 2 m 'Icosphere' at the origin that is not part of the rover: ignore it. The file carries animations: the mast animation (frames ~100-300) raises the mast, and that raised pose is used here (from_reference_model.mast_raised). The arm animations hold the stowed pose throughout, so the model has no deployed arm. Raised, the model agrees with Maki 2020: camera plate (Navcams) centre z 1.974 vs '~1.98 meters'; front Hazcams centre z ~0.75 vs '0.73 meters'; top of the mast head z 2.233 vs the press kit's 2.2 m tall.

arm_stowed.note: origins of the model's arm chain (arm.003 > arm.002 > arm > arm.004 > turret_obj), stowed across the front. Whether each origin sits on the real joint axis is unchecked; segment lengths from these: 0.82 m (joint 2 to elbow), 0.75 m (elbow to wrist). No document gives segment lengths (Moeller et al. 2021 could not be downloaded).

ground_clearance.note: WEB bottom z (see web_box). MSL's catalogue gives 'Clearance under the rover's body on flat ground is 66 cm.' (PDS hostMSL.cat, MSL not M2020): consistent.

mast_head_parts.note: NASA model's head at its mast animation frame 200, split into loose pieces and measured in the head's own frame: origin on the azimuth axis at the elevation pivot height (z 1.922), l along the head's facing (0.84, 0.54, 0), s along the elevation axis (-0.54, 0.84, 0), u up. Pieces by object: 'head' (SuperCam box, floor, centre block, drum), 'lens' (SuperCam window), 'NavCams', 'Mastcam_Z_cams'. Navcam centre u 0.056 puts the camera at z 1.978, agreeing with dimensions.navcam_height.

arm_end_parts.note: NASA model's stowed arm end (objects arm.003 shoulder, arm.001 and arm.004 wrist, turret_obj and PIXL turret), split into loose pieces; each entry is one large piece's world-axis bounds (box) or its axis and radius (cyl: round pieces whose two cross extents agree). The turret hub is rotated about 10 deg about z in the model; built axis-aligned. Instrument names are not in the model; only PIXL is (object PIXL). Keyed by the joint each group moves with.

hga_gimbal_parts.note: NASA model's antenna_hg object split into loose pieces: the plate (0.27 x 0.29 m at z 1.37-1.41, centre 0.391, 0.271) is carried by a gimbal arm (tilted piece, built axis-aligned) on a base cylinder and disc at (0.475, 0.46) on the deck. The post between disc and arm is not a separate piece in the model: est. to join them.

open_questions: Camera height conflict: Maki 2020 puts the Navcams at ~1.98 m, Bell 2021 puts Mastcam-Z (on the same plate, between the Navcams) at ~2.12 m. NASA's raised model agrees with Maki (1.974 m) and with the 2.2 m height. Proposed: follow Maki and the model; the 2.12 m stays recorded as a conflict.
Arm: only the stowed pose exists anywhere (the model's arm animation never moves). Proposed: model it stowed, segment lengths from the model.

MMRTG 64 cm diameter: with or without fins? The model's RTG object includes its cover and heat-exchanger panels, so it can't settle this. Proposed: model the covered assembly at the model's size and keep 64 x 66 cm for the bare unit inside.

Wheelbase, track, wheel width, deck height, pivot positions and arm segment lengths come only from the NASA model (no document found). Its documented sizes agree within a few percent, so this seems safe.

Markings not confirmed by NASA, left out: a NASA logo, the Mars 2020 mission logo on the rover (design press only), an 'insignia plate on the left front' (one search summary), the exact geocache text '221BBAKER' (Space.com only).

bake.note: Base colour projected from NASA's 3D model (nasa_3d_perseverance) with the mast raised (animation frame 200, as from_reference_model.mast_raised). Two passes: a near one (rays from 1.5 cm outside reaching 3.5 cm), then a far one (8 cm outside, 20 cm reach) for faces of stand-in shapes the near pass misses. A face missed by both keeps its sourced colour.
